Scheduler-membership metadata was not used to steer CLEAN scientific exploration.

bounded_slice.candidate: Freshness/rollback control for sa-replay-core-v1 using a two-version symbolic reference chain and one exact four-case matrix.
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Local deterministic symbolic replay of two versions only. D1 and D2 are symbolic expected digests rather than computed cryptographic outputs. The generation field is assumed to be included in the canonical projection for this freshness test. No public-source fetch, no actual hash/signature computation, no hosted verifier, no secret persistence, no protected/manual execution and no second semantic leaf.

reference_chain.trust_model: Digest validity authenticates exact projected content only when the expected digest is independently trusted. Generation ordering is meaningful for rollback rejection only when the verifier also holds an independently trusted freshness anchor outside the mutable record/chain.

matrix.reason: current content matches the independently trusted head digest and meets the trusted lower-bound generation
validity of D1 authenticates old content but cannot prove recency; trusted min_generation=2 rejects the stale-but-valid prior version
without an external expected digest or freshness lower bound, the verifier cannot distinguish current, stale, or substituted records
a mutable record cannot supply its own independent content or monotonic freshness anchor

minimum_freshness_result.observation: The stale-but-valid D1 case passes content validity by assumption yet fails only when compared with an independently trusted freshness anchor. A same-record generation value is insufficient for the same reason that a same-record digest is insufficient.
minimum_freshness_result.inference: For a verifier that already receives the exact current expected digest D2 from an independent trust channel, no separate monotonic datum is necessary to reject D1: the current expected digest itself acts as both content and freshness anchor. For a verifier that accepts any otherwise-valid version in an evolving reference chain, the minimum separate monotonic datum is one independently trusted lower bound on generation, min_accepted_generation=2, with generation bound into the canonical projection. A wall clock, hosted coordinator, secret persistence, or richer-mode executor is not required for this exact rollback decision.
minimum_freshness_result.chain_requirement: If predecessor links are used for auditability, predecessor_digest must also be content-bound. The chain alone does not create freshness: a stale prefix remains internally valid until compared with the external current-head digest or trusted minimum generation.
minimum_freshness_result.package_completeness: pass for the exact four-case symbolic rollback matrix and trust separation stated here; not a general cryptographic freshness proof
minimum_freshness_result.replayability: pass for deterministic case classification from presented generation/digest plus the independently trusted anchor; actual digest implementation not executed
minimum_freshness_result.hidden_executor_absence: pass for exact slice: local deterministic reasoning plus repository state/evidence transport only
minimum_freshness_result.quota_zero_assessment: The symbolic generation/digest comparisons require no hosted compute, cloud storage, paid model/API, artifact service, Codespaces, runner or finite credit. Repository transport is lightweight evidence/state transport; rate limits are handled by cross-invocation continuation rather than in-run waiting.
minimum_freshness_result.conflict_check: CLEAN-safe: only frozen sanitized controls and own scientist_agents LATEST/current checkpoint were semantically consumed. No O/downstream/other-worker/shared-ledger/protected/manual/scheduler semantics were consumed.
minimum_freshness_result.uncertainty: Not tested: cryptographic digest computation or collision resistance, canonicalizer interoperability, repository compromise, independent anchor distribution, authorization, key distribution, rotation/revocation, multi-writer generation allocation, fork resolution, threshold policy, clock-based expiry, signed Git verification or heterogeneous verifier cost.
